text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Backbenchers in parliament urged government to be cautious with the privatisation of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) to ensure there are no job losses.
- The government has urged donors to fulfil their pledges for the agricultural sector investment programme which it said is low.
- Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) secretary general Bingu Wa Mutharika has briefed a lawyer to challenge his suspension by the COMESA council of ministers.
- Bubonic plague, which has killed 30 people in southern Zambia over the past few weeks, has been brought under control, government officials said.
- Members of Parliament have proposed that government ministers be banned from entering into government contracts as it leads to abuse of office.
